title: test(schema-catalog): ratchet deprecated component types, and report why the div sweep cannot run as ruled
body:
Part of #3965

Authored by the `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49` (recorded here in prose because a body edit rewrites the footer to its bare form).

Lands the **closing lint** the 2026-08-29 ruling ordered, in ratchet form, and reports the measurement that says the **sweep half cannot run as specified**. #3965 remains open as the worklist carrier.

## Both of the card's headline numbers are wrong on today's ref

The card's own query was `grep -rl '"type": "div"' examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas | wc -l`, so **the 48 counted FILES**. Re-counted in that unit on `origin/main` @ `9486ac672`:

| unit | card (2026-08-09) | measured now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **files** (the card's unit) | 48 | **27** |
| nodes (occurrences) | not stated | **85** |
| corpus | 423 files | 431 files |

Positive control in the identical query shape: `"type": "card"` = **93 nodes / 53 files**, the same 93 measured on 08-10, 08-18 and 08-28. So the `div` drop is a real migration (#4003 moved 106 nodes), not a broken pattern.

The card's stated **symptom** is also already gone. It says "a deprecation warning per thumbnail". Rendering all 431 entries through the real `SchemaRenderer` with a `console.warn` spy active from the first entry:

```
entries_rendered=431  total_warns=4  div_deprecation_notices=1
```

One notice for the whole corpus — `DivRenderer` reports once per module load (#3998) and exempts `kind:'html'` nodes by provenance (#4000). The other three warns (react-i18next, a `visibleWhen` predicate, an expression failure) are the positive control that the spy was capturing, so `1` is a measurement rather than a silent spy. ⚠️ The first run of this census read `0`, because an earlier test in the same file had already latched the once-per-module-load guard; the number above is from an isolated file. A census that shares a module instance with any other `div` render is not measuring the corpus.

## Where the deprecation is declared, and why no fixture was swept

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/div.tsx`, as a `console.warn` string literal. It names `card` / `flex` / `container` / `stack` / `grid`. **None of them is a drop-in**, measured through the real `SchemaRenderer` on identical authored input `{ className: 'p-4', children: [...] }`:

(Angle brackets are spelled out as `TAG[classes]` below — this body is stored through a sanitizer that eats short tag-shaped fragments, backticks included.)

| type | wrapper | class attribute emitted | children |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `div` | `div` | `p-4` — the authored value, verbatim | inline |
| `container` | `div` | `w-full max-w-xl mx-auto sm:p-3 md:p-4 p-4` | inline |
| `flex` | `div` | `flex flex-row justify-start items-start gap-1.5 sm:gap-2 p-4` | inline |
| `stack` | `div` | `flex flex-col justify-start items-stretch gap-1.5 sm:gap-2 p-4` | inline |
| `grid` | `div` | `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 p-4` | inline |
| `card` | `div` | `rounded-lg border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-sm p-4` | wrapped in an **extra** `CardContent` element, `p-6 pt-0` |
| `section` | `section` | `p-4` — the authored value, verbatim | inline |

`div` is class-**transparent**; every replacement injects layout. Note `container`: `twMerge` does not strip the injected `sm:p-3 md:p-4`, because those are different responsive variants from the authored `p-4` — the box keeps the authored padding at base and silently gets **smaller** padding from `sm` up. And none of the 85 nodes authors a single layout prop (the only keys across all 85 are `type`, `className`, `children`, `body`) or carries a flex/grid display class, so there is no authored intent to carry across — the injection is pure addition.

The second difference is not cosmetic. `container` / `flex` / `stack` / `grid` render `schema.children` **only**; `div` renders `schema.children || schema.body`. Four of the 85 nodes author `body`. Measured on the real `basic-sidebar.json`, swapping only its `div`:

```
as authored (div)   elements=21  text="Menu…Settings Main content area"
swapped -> stack    elements=21  text="Menu…Settings"        <- content GONE
swapped -> flex     elements=21  text="Menu…Settings"        <- content GONE
swapped -> container / grid — same, content GONE
```

The element count is **unchanged at 21**, so the loss is invisible to any element-count check, and `catalog-gallery-render`'s `drewSomething` control still passes because the sidebar beside it draws. That is the silent catalog-wide regression a find-and-replace would have shipped — worse than the warning it removes, exactly as the dispatch warned.

`section` / `article` / `aside` are the one class-transparent family (`semantic.tsx` renders `Tag` with `className` and injects nothing, and reads `children || body`), so they are technically one-to-one — but they teach landmark elements as generic boxes across 27 exemplars, which is negative on the AI-authoring axis this card exists to protect. Three parties have now independently recommended against it (the 2026-08-09 implementing agent, the PM, and the 2026-08-28 dev); this makes four.

**No fixture was touched.** Under the 2026-08-25 escape clause the residue is excluded, and the 2026-08-29 ruling's own acceptance criterion — "browser spot-verification that renders are unchanged" — is the thing that cannot be met.

## What this PR does land

A catalog-scoped ratchet, `examples/schema-catalog/test/deprecated-component-types.test.ts`, delivering the ruling's stated purpose ("so the stock never regrows") in the only form that can ship before the sweep.

**Nothing stopped the 49th before this.** Both gates that touch component types ask only whether the type *resolves*, never whether it is deprecated — `catalog-gallery-render` asserts `ComponentRegistry.get(type)` is truthy (green today with all 85 deprecated nodes present), and `check-doc-component-types.mjs` walks `content/docs` and not `examples/**`. It is worse than the usual declared-but-unenforced shape: the deprecation is not declared anywhere **machine-readable** — `RegistryComponentMetaExtras` has no `deprecated` field, so the only statements of it are the `console.warn` literal and the label `'Container (Deprecated)'`. The gate therefore mirrors the list by hand and pins its own premise.

- Freezes the stock at **25 files / 80 nodes**; refuses a new file, refuses growth inside a baselined file, and refuses *removals left un-deducted* from the table (stale allowance would silently re-admit what a batch just removed).
- `span` is zero-tolerance — 0 nodes in this corpus at every ref measured, so nothing to grandfather.
- `components-basic-div/` (2 files / 5 nodes) is **exempt, not baselined**: that category *is* the migration guidance for this deprecation, shipping `use-card-instead` / `flex-layout` / `grid-layout` beside `nested-divs` / `custom-card`. Sweeping it would delete the before-and-after. Same class as `div.mdx`'s deliberate legacy examples. The exemption is checked for non-vacuity so it cannot become a hole nothing uses.
- Pins that `div.tsx` / `span.tsx` still declare their notices, so the hand-kept mirror dies loudly rather than outliving the deprecation.

The hand-kept mirror is a symptom, not a design choice: #6674 tracks giving the registry a machine-readable `deprecated` flag. If that lands, `DEPRECATED_TYPES` here derives from the registry instead of being mirrored, and the premise pin can be deleted.

27 files / 85 nodes = 25/80 baselined + 2/5 exempt.

## Verification

**Every arm goes RED against unfixed source** — committed first, each mutation proven on disk before reading any result, each restore pinned to `HEAD` and proven byte-identical:

| mutation | disk proof | gate | red arm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| new fixture outside the stock authors a `div` | injected-div-count=1 | exit 1 | *no fixture outside the frozen stock…* |
| baselined fixture gains a node | div-count 1→2 | exit 1 | *no baselined fixture grows…* |
| baselined fixture loses a node | div-count 1→0 | exit 1 | *the ratchet has no slack…* |
| a `span` appears | span-count=1 | exit 1 | *`span` is zero-tolerance…* |
| notice removed from `div.tsx` | notice-count 1→0 | exit 1 | *the deprecation this ratchet mirrors is still declared* |

Restore proof: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty, and HEAD-blob hash equality for both mutated files (empty hash treated as failure, not "nothing to compare"). Gate re-run on the restored tree: `Tests 7 passed (7)`, exit 0.

Also run, exit code captured **before** any pipe:

- `pnpm exec vitest run examples/schema-catalog/` — `Test Files 15 passed (15)`, `Tests 1853 passed (1853)`, exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the changed file — 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings. **Declared narrowing**: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` was not run. The population is read from eslint's own config, the file count off its `--format json` output, and the config is **not type-aware** (no `project:` / `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. CI runs the full farm regardless.
- `regenerate:check` — `src/index.ts is up to date (431 entries)`, exit 0.
- `check-changeset-presence.mjs` — its own verdict: *"No source of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."* `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — *"No changeset declares a `major` bump."* A changeset is included anyway, in the empty-frontmatter form AGENTS.md blesses for test-only changes, so "no release" is declared rather than inferred.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-schema-catalog run type-check` (objectui spells it with the hyphen) — exit **0**, zero `error TS` lines, after `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/example-schema-catalog^...' build` (exit 0). Run *before* that build it exits 2 with 37 errors, **0 of them naming this PR's file** — every one is `TS2307` / `TS2882` "cannot find module `@object-ui/*`" in files this PR does not touch, i.e. the unbuilt sibling `dist/*.d.ts` closure of a fresh worktree. Recorded because it is the trap, not a finding. The new file is genuinely in the program rather than silently excluded: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` hit = 1.

## What is not checked by anything

Thumbnail appearance. That is precisely why the renderer comparison above is the gate here and not the test suite — and why no fixture was swept.
